blocks.text: Sulfur dyes are synthesised by thionation or sulfurisation of organic compounds containing nitro or amino groups; the products contain sulfur linkages. They generally give black, brown, khaki, blue and green colours, for example sulfur black 1, sulfur blue and sulfur brilliant green.

blocks.prompt: How are sulfur dyes made, and what colours do they give?
blocks.explanation: By heating aromatic compounds containing nitro or amino groups with sulfur or sodium polysulfide (thionation), which builds sulfur linkages into the molecules; they give dark, inexpensive colours such as black, brown, khaki, blue and green.

items: Sulfur dyes: thionation of nitro- or amino-compounds; sulfur linkages; black, brown, khaki, blue, green (sulfur black 1, sulfur blue, sulfur brilliant green).
